### SynScan (SkyWatcher)

Devices: Telescope.

Protocol documentation: `AlpacaCore/external/SynScan/`. No external SDK required — uses serial communication directly.

Connection types: Serial (USB serial) only. Default 9600 baud, 8N1. Protocol versions V3 (older) and V4 (current).

- The connect samples the handset's binary `h` clock once unless a successful configured time write already established UTC. A failed sample leaves `UTCDate` unavailable (`InvalidOperation`) until a successful client write or reconnect; the getter performs no device exchange.

- Auto-detection scans `/dev/serial/by-id/` and `/dev/ttyUSB*` for SynScan hand controllers, probes each port with a firmware version query, and connects to the first responding mount.
- **Connect verifies the link with the protocol echo (`K` + byte → byte + `#`)** (issue #130): `connect()` only opens the port, so before this gate a port with nothing listening came up as `Connected=true` once every handshake query (firmware, model, site, time, RA/Dec, Alt/Az) had burnt its 5 s response timeout inside `catch (...)`, and every command then timed out too. Silence on the echo fails the connect within one timeout with a message naming the port. A mismatched reply is NOT accepted (PR #3 review: a port that merely answers something framed like the protocol would otherwise proceed into the swallowed handshake queries and reproduce the phantom link) — `echo_test()` first reads past it for the rest of one response timeout, because right after `connect_serial()` opens the port the first token can be a stale reply from the previous session (`connect_serial()` flushes the tty buffer, but a USB adapter's own FIFO can still deliver one), then resends the echo once for a handset that garbled a byte, and fails after a second mismatch. Regression tests for silence, garbled-once, garbled-twice and stale-token-ahead-of-echo are in `test_synscan_async_park.cpp`; the shared `FakeMountServer::default_responder()` answers the echo so the concurrency stress tests still connect (they assert it). `connected_` is atomic and `get_connected()` lock-free (the connect sequence holds `mutex_` throughout). Every handset command and reply is logged at TRACE (`HC <cmd> -> <reply>`; non-printable bytes as `\xNN`).
- **A silent handset is usually a wedged handset, not wiring** (EQM-35 Pro rig, SynScan V4 fw 04.40.00, 2026-09): after ANY bytes at the wrong baud (115200 from the Sky-Watcher direct-USB probe or a manual test) the handset answers nothing — both protocols, every baud, every DTR/RTS state — until power-cycled, and a mount restart does not reboot a handset that is USB-powered from the SBC (no re-enumeration in `dmesg` is the tell). Wrong-baud bytes are not the only way in (issue #881, same rig, handset firmware 06.03.00, PL2303GC adapter, 2026-10-07): with no other process on the port and only 9600 traffic, a handset power-cycled through the mount with its USB still plugged in answered at most one `K` echo (5 ms) and then nothing, and replugging the adapter alone did not revive it; what stops it is not established. Recovery, in this order: unplug the handset's USB from the SBC → power-cycle the mount → handset to its main screen → wait 30 s → plug USB back in. That sequence brought it back every time (`KB` and `KC` both answered, connect 0.54 s); power-cycling with the USB left in never did. Healthy, it answers `K`+byte with byte+`#` at 9600, auto-detect finds it (`HC firmware 04.40.00`), connect takes 0.6 s and reads 2–35 ms. Never send non-9600 traffic to a port that may be a handset; see `util/synscan_handset_probe.h`.
- **Pulse guiding**: SynScan V3/V4 protocol has no hardware pulse guide command. Driver implements software-timed variable-rate slew: issues a variable-rate axis slew, sleeps for the requested duration, then ends it. On the handset a variable-rate `P` slew is the motor's own speed and REPLACES tracking (EQM-35 Pro, HC 06.03.00, 2026-10-13: a 2 s west pulse sent as code 6 at 7.5"/s moved RA 50.6" east), so on an equatorial mount an RA move runs the motor westward at the base rate (sidereal while tracking, else 0) minus the eastward rate (`ra_motor_rate_locked`) and, while tracking, ends with the tracking command alone, which resumes sidereal at once with no stop in between (measured). The westward code is 7 at the southern rig; 6 is taken as westward north of the equator from INDI's SynScan driver (not measured on a northern mount). Dec has no tracking, so its rate is the move and it ends with a stop. `MoveAxis(0, 0)` while tracking sends the stop and then the tracking mode. A cancelled pulse (replacement, AbortSlew, teardown) still ends with a plain stop: AbortSlew restores tracking itself. `IsPulseGuiding` tracks completion via time-based end time plus delay.
- **GEM pier-side DEC direction flip**: DEC motor direction is inverted when the mount's pointing state is 'W' (west), matching the physical axis reversal on German equatorial mounts. This affects pulse guide and MoveAxis DEC commands.
- **Position override accumulation**: Instead of reading back noisy mount positions after tiny guide pulses, the driver accumulates expected `rate × duration` deltas in a private position estimate. All consecutive pulse guide directions (N/S/E/W) operate in the same coordinate baseline, eliminating drift between reads without changing the client's independent `TargetRightAscension` / `TargetDeclination` values or making unset targets readable.
- **RA tracking restoration**: a variable-rate stop leaves the RA motor stopped, so every RA move must end with the tracking mode while tracking. On an equatorial mount the pulse end and the landing move send `set_tracking_mode()` alone, which ends the move and resumes sidereal; on an Alt-Az mount, or an AZ-EQ mount whose geometry is not configured (`equatorial_geometry_locked()` false), the pulse stops the axis and then re-sends the mode, and the landing is finished with residual-aimed re-GOTOs instead of timed moves. `MoveAxis(0, 0)` stops and then re-sends the mode, and an RA `MoveAxis` drops the last known RA. Without this, the mount stops tracking after every RA pulse guide.
- **Tracking/alignment modes**: `T` modes are 0=off, 1=Alt-Az, 2=equatorial, 3=PEC mode (Sidereal + PEC), per the SynScan Serial Communication Protocol v3.3. There is no north/south pair (that is Celestron's numbering): the handset applies its own site, so equatorial tracking sends 2 in either hemisphere, and a southern site sending 3 put the handset into PEC playback. Select Alt-Az for AZ/DOB/AllView model IDs, otherwise EQ. Fixed EQ model IDs report `GermanPolar`; AZ-EQ IDs 5/6 are dual-mode and the handset does not expose the selected geometry, so the device config's `alignmentMode` (`altaz` or `equatorial`, issue #860) decides: Alt-Az, or `GermanPolar` with EQ tracking, and `SetPark`/`Park` follow it. With `alignmentMode` absent or `auto`, `AlignmentMode` and enabling tracking report an error rather than guess. For those unconfigured AZ-EQ mounts or an unavailable model ID, `SetPark` and `Park` keep the legacy RA/Dec fallback; this fallback cannot compensate RA for sidereal-time changes. Other model IDs ignore `alignmentMode`.
- **RA readback sawtooth and landing finish (issue #1030)**: the handset advances its local sidereal time once a second, so after a GOTO its precise RA readback (`e`) ramps down at sidereal rate and jumps up one second of RA (194 counts, 15") at each tick; the read right after the tick is the true value. Measured on the EQM-35 Pro (HC 06.03.00) with raw reads 0.23 s apart (the handset's own reply time): present from the first read after `L` reports done and steady for the 125 s observed; absent in the idle state before any GOTO; unchanged by a same-mode `T` re-send and by pulses. After every GOTO the driver hunts for the jump (`hunt_readback_tick_locked`, with Slewing still true; issue #1107: a hunt whose 1.3 s first-jump budget ends with no jump marks the handset sawtooth-free for the connection, later landings take one plain read, and connect/disconnect, a tracking write or a time write clear the mark): three jumps bracket the tick to about 30 ms, and the post-tick read plus the fraction since is the landing RA. `corrected_ra_hours_locked` corrects each precise RA read by the fraction of the second since the anchored tick for two minutes; a read inside the tick's uncertainty can fall on either side of it, one second apart, so the last known RA (landing, sync, pulse end) picks the side. An explicit tracking write, an `H` write and connect/disconnect drop the anchor; AbortSlew and MoveAxis drop only the last known RA. The handset also re-rolls every GOTO landing by a whole second of RA (two passes with an identical aim landed 194 counts apart) and lands a GOTO asked to move Dec by 16" or less 7" off on average (19" max), so a residual is never chased with another GOTO on an equatorial mount: the landing is finished with timed guide-rate moves (`nudge_axis_locked`, the pulse path's moves, see Pulse guiding), which the handset executes to 0.3" in Dec and within the readback's resolution in RA (ConformU 4.5.1 on `3de26c0a`: RA landings 0.45" off). A synchronous caller waits out the move on `motion_cv_` through the task clock, which every `motion_generation_` bump signals, so a superseding initiator returns it at once (issue #1108). At most `kMaxLandingRounds` rounds; a residual beyond `kNudgeMaxSeconds` of guide-rate motion gets one re-GOTO first. A landing beyond `kLandingRefineLimitArcsec` (600") is the handset's miss, not a residual (issue #1105: on the EQM-35 Pro, GOTOs to Dec -45 at HA -3 from HA +9 and at HA +3 from HA +4 ended 2,950-3,120" east, with the handset's own display agreeing, and a second GOTO to the same coordinates landed 0.5" off): it gets one repeat GOTO to the unchanged target, never one aimed by the residual, and a second miss that large throws `DriverException` (async: stored for `Slewing`). Not explained yet: a small GOTO sent a minute or more after the previous one took 52-55 s to report done and left RA at its start, while GOTOs sent within a second of the previous one moved normally.
- **Superseded sync slew**: the driver's blocking `slew_to_coordinates()` waits with the driver mutex released, so a concurrent motion command (AbortSlew, Park, another slew, or MoveAxis on either axis, including `MoveAxis(axis, 0)` on the other axis) bumps `motion_generation_` and the waiting slew throws `InvalidOperation` ("Slew superseded by a concurrent motion command") without writing the tracking mode over the new motion. The error does not prove the mount stopped; the hardware GOTO may still be running.
- **Getters and `DeviceState` are served from a polled snapshot, never from the handset** (issue #1247, [decision 0010](../../docs/decisions/0010-snapshot-served-state.md)). One status poll runs on an `AsyncOperation` slot for the life of the connection and fills `util::StateSnapshot<PolledFrame>`: every `kStatusPollPeriod` (1 s, start to start on the task clock, missed ticks skipped) it reads the slewing flag (`L`) and the equatorial pair (`e`), and every `kSlowPollEvery`-th tick also alt/az (`z`), pier side (`p`) and tracking mode (`t`). Sky-Watcher's 100 ms period is unsafe here: a hand-controller round trip is ~140 ms (issue #617) and a frame costs 2-5 of them. Position, Slewing, Tracking, pier side and `DeviceState` read the frame under the snapshot's leaf lock; `TimeStamp` is the frame's `measured_at` (`device_state_age()`). There is no position cache with a time-to-live any more. Control-path writes go through (`set_slewing_locked()`, `set_tracking_mode_cached_locked()`) so a read after a write sees it; a write that changes what the position means calls `drop_poll_in_flight_locked()` so an older sample is not published over it, and the end of a slew or park publishes a full frame (`publish_measurement_locked()`). Three failed ticks latch a link fault (getters throw `DriverException` "communications compromised", `Connected` stays true), a good tick clears it, and a fault standing past `util::kLinkStalenessBound` is a lost link ([decision 0009](../../docs/decisions/0009-link-loss-and-relink-policy.md)): `Connected` false, operations throw `NotConnected`, `DeviceState` is empty with no `TimeStamp`. The PulseGuide slew gate is the exception: it asks the handset (`get_slewing_locked(true)`), not the frame, so a keypad slew up to a second old still refuses the pulse. The readback-tick hunt takes `poll_hold_` under `mutex_`; a tick re-checks it under `mutex_` before its exchanges and the hunt waits for a tick already inside them (`poll_sampling_`), so no poll exchange widens the hunt's brackets. Tests: `test_synscan_telescope_snapshot.cpp`.
- **Park coordinate frame**: `SetPark` stores hour angle plus declination for equatorial models, not RA/Dec; Alt-Az models store azimuth/altitude. RA changes with local sidereal time for a fixed equatorial mechanical position, so `Park` reconstructs RA from current LST and the saved hour angle.
- Motion initiators are serialized across sync/async slews, park, PulseGuide, MoveAxis, AbortSlew, Unpark and disconnect. After its stop commands, every AbortSlew re-sends the currently requested tracking mode when tracking is on (`T` write), whether it stopped an RA pulse, a GOTO, a Park in flight or a MoveAxis, because the RA stop also stops sidereal tracking; an aborted Park therefore leaves the mount tracking, and a disabled tracking mode remains off. AbortSlew, MoveAxis, Unpark, Park and the slews do not cancel and join the slew body: each claims the slew slot under `mutex_` (`claim_slew_slot_locked()`, decision 0006 "Claim") and the body in flight becomes Superseded, so it touches no flag, target or axis once it has taken `mutex_` back after its current wire exchange. The bodies (async slew, Park, the landing hunt and nudges, `wait_for_slew_complete`) release `mutex_` around every wire exchange (`without_lock()`). Every motion command, from a body or an initiator (GOTOs, the park `T0` and failure stops, nudge move and stop, AbortSlew stops and restore, MoveAxis, Unpark's stop, the sync slew), goes out in an ordered wire turn (`WireTurn` / `send_in_turn()`): take a ticket under `mutex_`, wait for the turn with `mutex_` released, check at the turn that the sender still owns its operation, then send; a newer initiator's commands therefore always follow anything an older body is committed to send, and a superseded body sends nothing once it sees the claim (the landing nudge keeps the turn from its start command to its stop and always sends the stop). The Tracking write takes a ticket too but claims nothing: its `T` follows a stop and its tracking restore, so the requested mode is the one kept, and a write during a landing move waits for that move's stop (at most `kNudgeMaxSeconds` plus the stop exchanges). Getters and the status poll take no ticket. An initiator that sends a command of its own (MoveAxis, AbortSlew, Unpark during a Park) still waits for the one exchange in flight, because the protocol wrapper holds its mutex across it, but never for the old body. While a body owns the slot an initiator reads the tracking mode (`refresh_tracking_mode_locked()`) and the park position (`store_park_position_locked()`) from the cache and the polled frame. Disconnect, relink and the destructor still cancel and join. Tests: `test_synscan_initiator_supersede.cpp`. The async slew and Park bodies run on one `util::AsyncOperation` slot and each axis's pulse-guide stop timer on a slot of its own ([decision 0006](../../docs/decisions/0006-async-operation-ownership.md)); the driver has no raw `std::thread` member. An initiator whose claim superseded a body in flight and then has its `start()` refused stops the mount and publishes the AbortSlew state (`start_slew_body()`); a refused pulse-guide timer stops the axis it just started. The Park flow itself (dispatch, poll, settle, stop tracking, check the landing against the park target, publish) is `util::run_park_slew()` in `util/park_slew.h`, shared with Celestron; a landing beyond `kLandingRefineLimitArcsec` gets one repeat park GOTO and a second miss, or a landing read that throws, fails the park (`Slewing` throws `DriverException`, `AtPark` false). Once the stops succeed, AbortSlew clears the motion state (`Slewing`, pulse and manual-axis flags, stored slew error) before the tracking write, so a failed write throws `DriverException` with `Slewing` already false. A failed stop leaves the motion flags unchanged but stores an `AbortSlew stop failed` error, so `Slewing` continues to throw until a successful initiator; it still ends a Park in flight, whose superseded body no longer can, so Park can be called again. Park and Unpark stop failures likewise persist through `Slewing`.
- ConformU 4.3.0 validated for **Sky-Watcher HEQ5 PRO** on Linux arm64 with 0 errors and 0 issues.
